-- system_setting
CREATE TABLE system_setting (
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  value TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  UNIQUE(name)
);

-- user
CREATE TABLE user (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  created_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  updated_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  row_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (row_status IN ('NORMAL', 'ARCHIVED')) DEFAULT 'NORMAL',
  username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USER',
  email TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  nickname TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  avatar_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

-- user_setting
CREATE TABLE user_setting (
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  key TEXT NOT NULL,
  value TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE(user_id, key)
);

-- memo
CREATE TABLE memo (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  uid TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  creator_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  updated_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  row_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (row_status IN ('NORMAL', 'ARCHIVED')) DEFAULT 'NORMAL',
  content TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  visibility TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (visibility IN ('PUBLIC', 'PROTECTED', 'PRIVATE')) DEFAULT 'PRIVATE',
  pinned INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (pinned IN (0, 1)) DEFAULT 0,
  payload TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

-- memo_relation
CREATE TABLE memo_relation (
  memo_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  related_memo_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE(memo_id, related_memo_id, type)
);

-- attachment
CREATE TABLE attachment (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  uid TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  creator_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  updated_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  filename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  blob BLOB DEFAULT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  size INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  memo_id INTEGER,
  storage_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  reference TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  payload TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

-- idp
CREATE TABLE idp (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  uid TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  identifier_filter TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  config TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

-- inbox
CREATE TABLE inbox (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  created_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  sender_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  receiver_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  message TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

-- reaction
CREATE TABLE reaction (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  created_ts BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  creator_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  content_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  reaction_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE(creator_id, content_id, reaction_type)
);

-- memo_share
CREATE TABLE memo_share (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  uid        TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  memo_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  creator_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_ts BIGINT  NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  expires_ts BIGINT  DEFAULT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (memo_id) REFERENCES memo(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX idx_memo_share_memo_id ON memo_share(memo_id);

-- user_identity
CREATE TABLE user_identity (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  user_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  provider   TEXT    NOT NULL,
  extern_uid TEXT    NOT NULL,
  created_ts BIGINT  NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  updated_ts BIGINT  NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  UNIQUE (provider, extern_uid),
  UNIQUE (user_id, provider)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_user_identity_user_id ON user_identity(user_id);

All required information has been gathered.

The live browser event mechanism uses HTTP Server-Sent Events. The server endpoint is `GET /api/v1/sse`, registered via `RegisterSSERoutes` in `sse_handler.go`. The client-side implementation lives in `web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts`, which fetches from `/api/v1/sse` using `Accept: text/event-stream`, parses `data:` lines as JSON, and invalidates React Query caches. This hook is mounted in `web/src/main.tsx` through `AppInitializer`.

The hub implementation file is `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`. It defines the `SSEHub` struct with `Subscribe`, `Unsubscribe`, `Close`, and `Broadcast` methods. Supporting files include `sse_handler.go` for the HTTP endpoint and `sse_event_helpers.go` for event construction.

Direct SSE broadcasts are found in `memo_service.go`. `CreateMemo` emits `SSEEventMemoCreated` and `DeleteMemo` emits `SSEEventMemoDeleted`. The `CreateMemo` event is suppressed when triggered indirectly through `CreateMemoComment`.

`CreateMemoComment` in `memo_service_comments.go` emits `SSEEventMemoCommentCreated`.

`UpsertMemoReaction` and `DeleteMemoReaction` in `reaction_service.go` emit `SSEEventReactionUpserted` and `SSEEventReactionDeleted` respectively. Both use the `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent` helper.

`UpdateMemo` delegates to `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` to broadcast `SSEEventMemoUpdated`. `SetMemoAttachments` and `SetMemoRelations` also route through this helper to emit memo update events.

Share endpoints run on separate RPCs and never broadcast SSE events. Attachment, relation, and comment handlers are all part of the memo service RPC surface and do broadcast. Reactions and comments use dedicated event types, but attachments and relations piggyback on the generic `memo.updated` event through the side effects helper.

## Live browser event mechanism

```24:30:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go
// RegisterSSERoutes registers the SSE endpoint on the given Echo router.
func RegisterSSERoutes(router sseRouteRegistrar, hub *SSEHub, storeInstance *store.Store, secret string) {
	authenticator := auth.NewAuthenticator(storeInstance, secret)
	router.GET("/api/v1/sse", func(c *echo.Context) error {

	})
}
```

```66:77:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go
func (s *APIV1Service) dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects(ctx context.Context, memo *store.Memo, parentMemo *store.Memo, memoMessage *v1pb.Memo) {
	if err := s.DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to dispatch memo updated webhook", slog.Any("err", err))
	}

	s.SSEHub.Broadcast(&SSEEvent{
		Type:       SSEEventMemoUpdated,
		Name:       memoMessage.Name,
		Parent:     memoMessage.GetParent(),
		Visibility: memo.Visibility,
		CreatorID:  resolveSSECreatorID(memo, parentMemo),
	})
}
```

## Do attachment / relation / reaction / comment / share handlers count?

| Category | Counts? | Rationale |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Comment** (`CreateMemoComment`) | **Yes** | Dedicated memo-service RPC; broadcasts `memo.comment.created`. Internal `CreateMemo` call is SSE-suppressed. |
| **Reaction** (`UpsertMemoReaction`, `DeleteMemoReaction`) | **Yes** | Memo-service RPCs; broadcast `reaction.upserted` / `reaction.deleted` (memo content IDs). |
| **Attachment** (`SetMemoAttachments`) | **Yes (indirect)** | Memo-service RPC; broadcasts via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` as `memo.updated`. Standalone `AttachmentService` handlers do **not** broadcast. |
| **Relation** (`SetMemoRelations`) | **Yes (indirect)** | Same pattern as attachments — `memo.updated` via helper. |
| **Share** (`CreateMemoShare`, `ListMemoShares`, `DeleteMemoShare`, `GetMemoByShare`) | **No** | No `SSEHub` / `Broadcast` / `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` references in `memo_share_service.go`. |

**Summary:** 9 production broadcast paths across 8 distinct RPC handler methods (+ 1 shared helper). All are on `MemoService` except reactions, which are also `MemoService` RPCs in `reaction_service.go`. Share handlers are memo-adjacent but do not participate in live refresh.

`dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` loads webhooks via `Store.GetUserWebhooks`, converts the memo to a payload, and calls `webhook.PostAsync` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. That method enqueues the request asynchronously. Workers then execute `Post`, which signs the payload with HMAC-SHA256 and sends the HTTP POST via `safeClient.Do` using `net/http`.

The signing key is either raw secret bytes or base64-decoded from a `whsec_` prefix. The signed payload concatenates `msgID + " + timestamp + "." + body`, where `msgID` is `"msg_" + uuid`, timestamp is a Unix seconds string, and body is JSON-marshaled. Request headers include `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` formatted as `v1,<base64(HMAC-SHA256)>`. Content-Type is `application/json`.

The exact dispatch function is `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`. It delegates to `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`, which fetches user webhooks and calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)`. The payload excludes `signingSecret` because its JSON tag is `-`. The caller is `CreateMemo` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` at line 157.

`PostAsync` lives in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` and enqueues to an async worker queue. Workers call `Post`, which uses `net/http` to send the request. The signing algorithm is HMAC-SHA256. The signing key comes from `resolveSigningKey`, decoding a `whsec_` prefix or using raw bytes. The signed message is `msgID + "." + timestamp + "." + JSON_body`. The headers are `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` formatted as `v1,base64(HMAC)`.

Signature headers are omitted entirely when SigningSecret is empty. The exact package path is `github.com/usememos/mes/internal/webhook`. `CreateMemo` also invokes `dispatchMemoMentionNotificationsBestEffort`, but that path handles user notifications rather than webhooks.

## Memo-created webhook trace

### 1. What `CreateMemo` calls

`CreateMemo` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` invokes **`DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`** after the memo is persisted and converted to a protobuf message:

```156:159:server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go
	// Try to dispatch webhook when memo is created.
	if err := s.DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to dispatch memo created webhook", slog.Any("err", err))
	}
```

**Dispatch function:** `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`  
**File:** `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`

```14:16:server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go
// DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook dispatches a webhook when a memo is created.
func (s *APIV1Service) DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook(ctx context.Context, memo *v1pb.Memo) error {
	return s.dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook(ctx, memo, "memos.memo.created")
```

That delegates to **`dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`** in the same file, which:

1. Resolves the memo creator via `ResolveUserByName`
2. Loads the creator’s configured webhooks via `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(ctx, creatorID)` (`store/user_setting.go`)
3. Builds a `webhook.WebhookRequestPayload` with `activityType = "memos.memo.created"`, plus each hook’s `Url` and `SigningSecret`
4. Enqueues dispatch with **`webhook.PostAsync(payload)`**

```48:72:server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go
func (s *APIV1Service) dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook(ctx context.Context, memo *v1pb.Memo, activityType string) error {
	creator, err := ResolveUserByName(ctx, s.Store, memo.Creator)
	// ...
	webhooks, err := s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(ctx, creatorID)
	// ...
	for _, hook := range webhooks {
		payload, err := convertMemoToWebhookPayload(memo)
		// ...
		payload.ActivityType = activityType
		payload.URL = hook.Url
		payload.SigningSecret = hook.SigningSecret

		// Use asynchronous webhook dispatch
		webhook.PostAsync(payload)
	}
	return nil
}
```

---

### 2. Where the HTTP request is sent

**Package:** `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/webhook`  
**File:** `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

- **`PostAsync`** enqueues the payload on `asyncPostQueue`; four background goroutines drain the queue and call **`Post`**.
- **`Post`** constructs and sends the actual HTTP request via Go’s **`net/http`** client (`safeClient.Do(req)`).

```119:152:internal/webhook/webhook.go
// Post posts the message to webhook endpoint.
func Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error {
	body, err := json.Marshal(requestPayload)
	// ...
	req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, bytes.NewBuffer(body))
	// ...
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	// ... signing headers if secret present ...
	resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)
```

```182:196:internal/webhook/webhook.go
// PostAsync posts the message to webhook endpoint asynchronously.
func PostAsync(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) {
	// ...
	select {
	case asyncPostQueue <- requestPayload:
	default:
		slog.Warn("Dropped webhook dispatch because the async queue is full", ...)
	}
}
```

**Request body shape** (from `WebhookRequestPayload` JSON tags): `url`, `activityType`, `creator`, `memo`. `SigningSecret` is excluded from JSON (`json:"-"`).

---

### 3. Request signing (evidenced)

Signing follows the **Standard Webhooks** pattern (explicitly referenced in comments and tests). It runs only when `SigningSecret != ""`.

**Key derivation** (`resolveSigningKey`):

- If secret starts with `whsec_`: base64-decode the suffix to raw key bytes.
- Otherwise: use the secret string as raw bytes.

```92:106:internal/webhook/webhook.go
func resolveSigningKey(secret string) ([]byte, error) {
	if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(secret, "whsec_"); ok {
		decoded, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(rest)
		// ...
		return decoded, nil
	}
	return []byte(secret), nil
}
```

**Algorithm and signed content** (`Post`):

- **Algorithm:** HMAC-SHA256 (`crypto/hmac` + `crypto/sha256`)
- **Signed message:** `msgID + "." + timestamp + "." + body`
  - `msgID` = `"msg_"` + UUID
  - `timestamp` = Unix seconds as decimal string (`strconv.FormatInt(time.Now().Unix(), 10)`)
  - `body` = JSON-marshaled payload bytes
- **Signature encoding:** standard base64 of the HMAC digest

**Headers set:**

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `webhook-id` | `msg_<uuid>` |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Unix timestamp string |
| `webhook-signature` | `v1,<base64(HMAC-SHA256)>` |

```133:149:internal/webhook/webhook.go
	if requestPayload.SigningSecret != "" {
		key, err := resolveSigningKey(requestPayload.SigningSecret)
		// ...
		msgID := "msg_" + uuid.New().String()
		timestamp := strconv.FormatInt(time.Now().Unix(), 10)

		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
		mac.Write([]byte(msgID + "." + timestamp + "."))
		mac.Write(body)
		signature := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))

		req.Header.Set("webhook-id", msgID)
		req.Header.Set("webhook-timestamp", timestamp)
		req.Header.Set("webhook-signature", "v1,"+signature)
	}
```

This is verified end-to-end in `internal/webhook/webhook_test.go` (`TestPostSignsRequest`), which recomputes the same HMAC over `gotID + "." + gotTimestamp + "." + gotBody` and expects `webhook-signature` = `"v1," + base64(...)`. If no secret is configured, no signature headers are sent (`TestPostWithoutSecretSetsNoSignatureHeaders`).

```
CreateMemo (memo_service.go)
  → DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook (memo_service_webhooks.go)
    → dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook (activityType: "memos.memo.created")
      → Store.GetUserWebhooks (store/user_setting.go)
      → webhook.PostAsync (internal/webhook/webhook.go)
        → Post (async worker)
          → net/http POST to hook.Url
```

The full picture is now clear.

The Echo HTTP server launches via a goroutine in `server/server.go:124-128`, triggered by `server.Start()`. The S3 presign runner is a one-shot job in `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`; it runs synchronously inside `startBackgroundRunners()` at `server/server.go:163` before the main loop goroutine begins.

The S3 presign runner also runs periodically. A goroutine starts at `server/server.go:167-169` and loops via `time.NewTicker(12*time.Hour)`, so the first tick fires after twelve hours.

Three store cache cleanup loops run via `time.NewTicker(CleanupInterval)` where `CleanupInterval` is five minutes. They launch inside `store.New()` at `main.go:64` before `server.Start()`. The three instances are `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, and `userSettingCache`.

Four webhook dispatch workers spawn in `internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-54` via `init()`. Each blocks on a buffered `asyncPostQueue` channel of capacity 128.

Two email send workers start in `internal/email/email.go:16-35` through `init()`. They consume a buffered `asyncEmailQueue` of capacity 128.

A signal-shutdown goroutine waits on SIGINT and SIGTERM in `cmd/memos/main.go:99-103`.

SSE heartbeat tickers run per HTTP connection on a request-driven timer. PAT usage updates spawn fire-and-forget goroutines per authentication request. The scheduler timeout middleware launches a goroutine only when the scheduler is actually used. gRPC-gateway connection close goroutines run per registration.

The internal scheduler package contains a full cron scheduler, yet it is never imported outside its own package in production code.

`server/runner/memopayload` defines `NewRunner` and `RunOnce`, yet it is never wired into `startBackgroundRunners`; `RebuildMemoPayload` is only called inline during memo creation and updates.

Workers will be grouped into three categories: those launched directly inside `server.Start()` or `startBackgroundRunners()`, those started earlier in the main startup path such as `store.New()`, and process-level `init()` workers that remain alive without being explicitly started by server code.

The email and webhook workers are process-level `init()` goroutines. The server binary loads them automatically because the server imports the email package and the API v1 package, which transitively imports the webhook package.
